subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements regarding the ***PM Poshan Shakti Nirman Scheme***:

Statement 1: The PM Poshan Shakti Nirman Scheme replaced the Mid Day Meal Scheme.

Statement 2: The nutritional norms for the scheme specify 450 calories, 12g protein, and 100g food grains for primary school children.

Statement 3: The scheme covers children up to class X in government and government-aided schools.

Which of the above statements are ***correct***?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct.**__

__
 
• **Statement 1 is correct** because the **PM Poshan Shakti Nirman Scheme, launched in 2021, replaced the Mid Day Meal Scheme **with the goal of providing nutritious meals to children in government and government-aided schools.
 
• **Statement 2 is correct** because the nutritional norms for primary school children under this scheme include 450 calories, 12g protein, and 100g food grains, which help meet the nutritional needs of young students.
 
• **Statement 3 is incorrect** because **the scheme covers children up to class VIII**, not class X. It specifically targets children in pre-primary (Balvatika) and classes I to VIII in government and government-aided schools.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **In News__**

__
 
• **The Centre has increased the allocation for the PM Poshan Shakti Nirman Scheme to ₹12,500 crore for the financial year 2025-26, reflecting a 25% increase from the previous year.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **PM Poshan Scheme:** Launched in 2021, the scheme replaced the Mid Day Meal Scheme to provide nutritious meals to children in government and government-aided schools.
 
• Class Coverage: The scheme covers children from pre-primary (Balvatika) to class VIII, and its main objective is to encourage school attendance and improve children's health and education outcomes.
 
• **Coverage:** The scheme benefits over 11.20 crore children across 11.20 lakh schools in India, with a focus on improving school attendance and retention, especially for disadvantaged children.
 
• **Nutritional Norms:**
 
 
• **Primary**: 450 calories, 12g protein, 100g food grains, 20g pulses, 50g vegetables, 5g oil & fat.
 
• **Upper Primary**: 700 calories, 20g protein, 150g food grains, 30g pulses, 75g vegetables, 7.5g oil & fat.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Increased Budget:** For FY 2025-26, the scheme's allocation has been increased to ₹12,500 crore, a 25% rise from the previous year, reflecting the government’s commitment to enhancing the scheme's reach and effectiveness.
 
• **Material Cost Hike:** The material cost for meals has been raised by 9.5%, resulting in an additional central expenditure of ₹954 crore for the scheme in FY 2025-26.
 
• **PM Poshan’s Impact:** By providing nutritious meals, the scheme aims to improve the nutritional status of children, increase school attendance, and enhance learning outcomes, helping children concentrate better in classrooms.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Key Objectives:**

 
 
• **Nutritional Improvement:** Improve the nutritional status of children.
 
• **School Attendance:** Encourage regular school attendance and retention, particularly among disadvantaged children.
 
• **Learning Outcomes:** Enhance concentration and learning by addressing classroom hunger.
 
 

69:T
